g.text: NEGOTIATION LEVERS · PROPOSALS AFTER SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS
Two proposal packagessupported by the analysis
Both proposals preserve an 8% preferred return. Package A removes catch-up while keeping 20% carry.Package B retains catch-up and reduces carry to 15%.

Common terms: the offered 1.35% fee; return of LP contributed capital (including contributions used for fees) before carry;an 8% annual preferred return compounded on unreturned capital and unpaid preferred return. Preserve any stronger existing protection.
Standard-hurdle value
Further improvement
Reference: 8% hurdle · full catch-up · 20% carry
Package A: 8% hurdle · no catch-up · 20% carry
Package B: 8% hurdle · full catch-up · 15% carry
If TPG VI already has thereference hurdle, only thecolored gains are new:
Conditional illustration; the actualLPA is unverified.
A adds $20.65m and B $19.31m over the common baseline — a difference of $1.33m. The negotiating order comes next.

OPERF inception NPV; 20% asset growth; 15% discount rate. Baseline: 1.35% fee, 20% carry, no hurdle.Package values depend on the scenario; actual amendments require forward valuation. The bars are alternatives, not cumulative demands.

Source: Q5 Analysis!D10 (reference), C10 (A), G10 (B); increments C10 − D10 = 17.920340 and G10 − D10 = 16.587284. Package B keeps the hurdle, so its total($19.31m) exceeds the isolated 15%-carry scenario ($17.67m). Metrick & Yasuda (2007) and the Apollo S-1 (2008) supply the contemporary context.
